claims.text: At stage-3 Notifications is a separate service; ADR 0002 line 43 lists its running costs: one more image, build pipeline, database and dashboard.
At stage-2 order emails were a module inside DonHang.Api (QueuedNotifier, NotificationSender in every API copy).

A merge is worth weighing when services act as a distributed monolith that moving shared logic or data to one side does not fix, when the split's reason has gone, or when running apart costs more than independence returns; while the drivers hold, keeping is the default.

A merge's own costs: the separate database is moved into the other database or kept apart and used by the module in one process; the boundary the network held must then be held by the compiler and tests.

Merging back as a module with its contract and own data kept leaves splitting out again cheap; folding the code into Ordering with no boundary means a new extraction after cutting shared classes and tables.

ADR 0002 options (lines 28-34): keep email as a module in DonHang.Api (no extra cost, but other services go through the API and email failures stay in the order-taking process) vs a separate service with donhang_notifications reached over RabbitMQ.

ADR 0002 lines 17-21 give two drivers: Payments must also message customers, and email server failures should stay out of the order-taking process; lines 23-24: the number of API copies alone was not enough reason to split.
ADR 0002 lines 46-47: the old notifications table stayed in donhang, unread, recorded as debt N1 in tech-debt-register.md with ADR 0008, which deals with deleting the two old tables.

docs/adr/README.md lines 39-46: a rejected ADR is still merged and kept so the idea is not re-proposed without a new reason; an accepted ADR is not rewritten, the old one only gets status 'Bị thay thế bởi NNNN' with a link.
ADR 0002's status is on line 3; a supersede changes only that line, to 'Bị thay thế bởi' with the new number and a link.
As a separate service, Notifications stopping does not stop orders being placed; messages wait in the queue (ADR 0002 lines 31-34).

At stage-3 DonHang.Api holds two modules, Ordering and Catalog (reached only through its contract: ICatalog plus two other public types ModuleBoundaryTests lists); the compiler stops other projects naming Catalog's internal types, and ModuleBoundaryTests fail on forbidden references.

claims.text: Choices: merge as a module when no other service messages customers and the email server itself no longer slows or fails; treat changes in step as a distributed-monolith sign first, keeping the service while drivers hold; keep it when running cost is the only complaint.
A merge is recorded in a new ADR that supersedes 0002; 0002 keeps its reasons and only its status changes, so the new ADR can name which driver stopped holding.
